tools.name: library_create
tools.description: Create a library: a named, saved subset of interventions — on a topic, in a period, of a group — from one or SEVERAL countries, for focused and comparative analysis. Each country gets its own definition (terms, filters, time window), recorded with the edition of the data. Returns the description of what was gathered (see library_describe). Then pass library=<name> to any analysis tool. Equivalent terms across countries are the user's claim: say so when reporting.

params.name: name
params.description: Library name (case-insensitive)

params.name: countries
params.description: ISO2 codes of the chambers it takes (one or several)

params.name: terms
params.description: An intervention enters if it uses ANY of these: comma- or '+'-separated, '*' ends a prefix, whole words, case- and accent-insensitive. Give Spanish AND Portuguese forms when BR or PT are in ('corrupción+corrupção')

params.name: regex
params.description: terms is one RE2 regular expression

params.name: min_occurrences
params.description: Times the terms must appear in the intervention: 2-3 keeps those that DISCUSS the topic, not those that mention it

params.name: date_from
params.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: date_to
params.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive)

params.name: party
params.description: Party label as an ILIKE pattern, e.g. 'PSOE' or '%Frente%'

params.name: sex
params.description: Speaker's sex (linked deputies only)

params.name: speech_only
params.description: Only rows with dm_speech = 1 (recommended)

params.name: exclude_chair
params.description: Leave out the presiding officer's turns (procedural speech: giving the floor, calling votes)

params.name: max_turn_words
params.description: Leave out turns longer than this many words — mostly documents read into the record; 10000 is a sensible check

params.name: event_dates
params.description: Align on an event: {ISO2: 'YYYY-MM-DD'} per country; each country's window becomes event − days_before … event + days_after (stored as plain dates). To find the dates: term_counter (first use per chamber) or term_frequency(by='session')

params.name: per_country
params.description: Per-country overrides of the settings above, e.g. {'BR': {'terms': 'aborto+interrupção da gravidez'}, 'ES': {'date_from': '2010'}}

tools.description: Bring libraries made in the Diarios Explorer into the MCP — several countries' files become one comparative library. Every item is checked against the loaded data (row → intervention, then its date and speaker); whatever does not match is reported, not translated silently.

tools.name: cooccurrence_network
tools.description: Network of WORDS of a library and its themes: the library's characteristic words and expressions (its lexicon against the rest of the country's corpus), joined when they occur in the same intervention (or fragment) more than chance (signed G², each term's k strongest neighbours, weight = observed/expected), clustered by Leiden into themes. Per theme: terms, coverage, words of the parties (per 1,000 of their words) and the interventions to read first. The Diarios Explorer's method, ported and tested against its code. Writes an interactive HTML, CSV, JSON and a summary. One network per country. Not for people or institutions (comention_network) nor for who names whom (mention_network).

params.name: library
params.description: Library name (the network is built on its interventions)

params.name: vocabulary
params.description: Terms of the library's lexicon used as nodes (the most over-used against the rest of the corpus)

params.name: unit
params.description: Unit of context: the whole intervention, or consecutive fragments of `fragment` tokens

params.name: neighbours
params.description: Each term keeps its k strongest edges (by G²)

params.name: resolution
params.description: Leiden resolution γ: higher, more and smaller themes (0.6 / 1 / 1.6 in the explorer)

params.name: exclude
params.description: Terms to leave out after reading the themes (any case or accents)

params.name: expressions
params.description: Join the corpus's multi-word expressions ('reforma da previdência') into one node (tables of the Diarios Explorer, downloaded once and checked against the loaded dataset)

params.name: speech_only
params.description: Leave out stage directions in brackets and upper-case lines (vote lists, headers)

params.name: date_from
params.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD

params.name: date_to
params.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive)

params.name: exclude_chair
params.description: Leave out the presiding officer's turns (procedural speech: giving the floor, calling votes)

params.name: max_turn_words
params.description: Leave out turns longer than this many words — mostly documents read into the record; 10000 is a sensible check

params.name: output_dir
params.description: ABSOLUTE folder for the files

params.name: formats
params.description: Files to write in output_dir (default all four)

params.name: max_node_size
params.description: Largest node radius in the page, in px on screen (nodes keep their size when zooming); the page has a control

params.name: max_edge_width
params.description: Widest line in the page, in px (lines stay thin: weights are read in the tooltips and tables)

params.name: layout
params.description: Layout the page opens with (it can be switched there): 'force'; 'clusters', each group (theme, community, party) as a separate disc, kept apart; 'rings', the Diarios Explorer's centrifugal layout: rings by number of connections (the most connected in the centre), sectors by group

summary.es: Red de palabras de una biblioteca y sus temas: sus palabras características que aparecen juntas, agrupadas con Leiden.
summary.en: A word network of a library and its themes: its characteristic words that occur together, clustered with Leiden.

example.es: ¿De qué temas se habló en la biblioteca «agua» de Chile y qué partidos los usan más?
example.en: Which themes run through the Chilean 'agua' library, and which parties use them most?

tools.name: comention_network
tools.description: Network of ACTORS (people and institutions) mentioned in the same intervention of a library: co (volume), NPMI (affinity), Jaccard, counts by group and each actor's bias between two groups, Leiden communities, centralities, examples (KWIC) and ambiguity warnings. Writes an interactive HTML (light/ dark, accessible, with tables), CSV, JSON and a summary. One network per country. Without `entities` it proposes candidates (proper names, acronyms) and builds nothing until you confirm them. Words and ideas are not actors: their network is cooccurrence_network.

params.name: library
params.description: Library name (the network is built on its interventions)

params.name: entities
params.description: Actors [{name, type: persona|institucion, pattern, exclude?}]: people and institutions only (words and ideas are cooccurrence_network's nodes). pattern and exclude are regular expressions (RE2: no look-arounds) over lower-case, accent-free text, e.g. '\bsupremo tribunal|\bstf\b'. A match inside `exclude`, or inside a LONGER match of another actor, does not count ('maria pereira' is not 'pereira'). Omit to get candidates first.

params.name: groups
params.description: Up to two contrast groups of labels of `group_by`, e.g. {'left': ['PT', 'PSOL'], 'right': ['PL']}; every other label is 'rest'. Case-insensitive. No default: the classification is yours

tools.name: mention_network
tools.description: Directed network of who mentions whom in a library: an arrow speaker → deputy (or external actor) counts the speaker's interventions that name them. Names come from the deputies register (in office on the day), by full name anywhere or by surname after a title; homonyms are resolved by the title's gender and the party written next to the name, otherwise listed apart (never guessed). The record's notes in brackets are not counted. Gives in/out strength, PageRank, reciprocity, Leiden communities, a group → group matrix, E-I and asymmetric pairs, and writes an interactive HTML (network and heat map, with tables), CSV, JSON and a summary. One network per country.

params.name: target_scope
params.description: Who can be mentioned: deputies of the chamber, the external actors given, or both

params.name: external_actors
params.description: People or bodies outside the chamber to count as targets: [{name, aliases: [...], role}]. They are matched first, by any alias, so declaring a homonym of a deputy (a minister, a former adviser) also keeps it from being taken for the deputy

params.name: mention_kinds

tools.name: theme_dossier
tools.description: The evidence to READ the themes of a word network, so that a theme is more than a list of words. It rebuilds what the network read and proves it (every theme's interventions equal the file's), then gives per theme: core and bridge terms, links to other themes, who sustains it (speakers, sessions: a theme held by one debate is an episode), its profile by year, the words each group says more inside it (a first hint of frames), its stability when Leiden is re-run, and a reading sample stratified by group and year with passages cut from the record. Writes the dossier (JSON, Markdown) and a codebook template; read each theme with theme=k, fill the codebook (verdict, label, definition, anchors with verbatim quotes, frames with stance) and check it with check_codebook. Method: parlaibero://methods/networks § 4.

params.name: network
params.description: ABSOLUTE path of the <library>_words.json that cooccurrence_network wrote (one per country)

params.name: theme
params.description: A theme's number, as in the page: its full dossier, with the reading sample and its passages. Omit for the overview of all themes (and the files)

params.name: sample
params.description: Interventions per theme in the reading sample, one per group and year in turn, after the 3 the network ranks first

params.name: passages
params.description: Passages per intervention, around the densest clusters of the theme's words

params.name: window
params.description: Words on each side of the theme's words

params.name: group_by
params.description: Column of the groups compared inside each theme (party, sex…)

params.name: stability_runs
params.description: Leiden re-runs with other seeds on the saved graph

params.name: seed
params.description: Seed of the reading sample

params.name: output_dir
params.description: ABSOLUTE folder; default the network file's

summary.es: La evidencia para leer cada tema de una red de palabras: quién lo sostiene, su perfil por año, las palabras de cada grupo dentro del tema, su estabilidad y pasajes del acta. Escribe una plantilla de codebook.
summary.en: The evidence to read each theme of a word network: who sustains it, its profile by year, the words each group says inside it, its stability and passages from the record. Writes a codebook template.

example.es: Prepara la lectura de los temas de la red de «agua» de Chile, por partido, y enséñame el dossier del tema 2.
example.en: Prepare the reading of the themes of the Chilean 'agua' network, by party, and show me theme 2's dossier.

tools.name: check_codebook
tools.description: Checks a codebook of themes and frames written after reading theme_dossier: its schema and theme numbers, and every anchor against the record (the id exists and is in the library; the quote appears verbatim; it holds the theme's words). Writes a blind sample of passages (no group, no theme) with two empty coding files, one for a person and one for the agent, who codes in a fresh context without the key or the dossier; with both filled (human=, agent=) it gives their agreement (Cohen's κ) and each theme's and frame's share of the coded passages, overall and by group, with Wilson intervals. Method: parlaibero://methods/networks § 4.

params.name: codebook
params.description: ABSOLUTE path of the codebook that theme_dossier wrote, filled

params.name: sample_size
params.description: Passages in the blind sample to code, allocated to the groups in proportion to their size

params.name: seed
params.description: Seed of the sample: the same seed draws the same sample

params.name: human
params.description: ABSOLUTE path of the sample coded by a person

params.name: agent
params.description: ABSOLUTE path of the same sample coded by the agent

params.name: group_by
params.description: Column of the groups (party, sex…)

params.name: output_dir
params.description: ABSOLUTE folder; default the codebook's

params.name: overwrite
params.description: Replace the sample and coding files (they may hold codes)

summary.es: Comprueba literalmente contra el acta las citas del codebook que escribe el agente, y saca una muestra ciega para medir su acuerdo con una persona (κ de Cohen).
summary.en: Checks verbatim against the record the quotes of the codebook the agent writes, and draws a blind sample to measure its agreement with a person (Cohen's κ).

example.es: Comprueba el codebook de «agua» y prepárame la muestra ciega de 60 pasajes para codificarla.
example.en: Check the 'agua' codebook and prepare the blind sample of 60 passages for me to code.

tools.name: theme_report
tools.description: The last step of reading a word network's themes: a report that interprets them for the researcher. Without `report` it writes a spec template (JSON) listing the quotable anchors and every figure as a placeholder; you write the interpretation in it (title, lede, findings, a paragraph after each figure, the themes in blocks with their frames and quotes, caveats, next steps). With `report` it checks the spec (every figure is a placeholder the engine fills, every quote an anchor of the codebook found verbatim in the record now, every codable theme in the report once; bare numbers, missing caveats and names are warned) and, without errors, writes the report as Markdown and HTML (three figures with their tables, the seat of every quote, what is measured and what is reading, the method and the citation) and a _check.json. It refuses a codebook with merge or split verdicts or a network that no longer matches. No language model runs here: the prose is yours. Method: parlaibero://methods/networks § 4.

params.name: codebook
params.description: ABSOLUTE path of the filled codebook (checked with check_codebook)

params.name: report
params.description: ABSOLUTE path of the report spec with your interpretation. Omit it to write the spec template next to the codebook

params.name: group_by
params.description: Column of the groups in the figures (party, sex…); a spec keeps its own

params.name: language
params.description: Language of the report; default the country's

params.name: output_dir
params.description: ABSOLUTE folder; default the codebook's (template) or the spec's (report)

params.name: overwrite
params.description: Replace the spec template (it may hold your text)

summary.es: El informe que interpreta los temas para quien investiga, en .md y .html: el agente escribe el texto y el motor pone las cifras, vuelve a comprobar las citas y dibuja tres figuras con sus tablas.
summary.en: The report that interprets the themes for the researcher, as .md and .html: the agent writes the prose, and the engine fills the figures, checks the quotes again and draws three figures with their tables.

example.es: Escribe el informe de los temas de «agua»: qué es cada tema, cuánto pesa, en qué años y partidos, y cómo se argumenta, con citas.
example.en: Write the report on the 'agua' themes: what each theme is, how much it weighs, in which years and parties, and how it is argued, with quotes.
